name: text-reveal
summary: Headings rise, slide up, fade, pop or type into place letter by letter, word by word or line by line.
looks: When the text scrolls into view, each letter, word or line rises from a little below its baseline, standing up from a backward tilt and coming into focus as it fades in, one after another in reading order; other motions slide each one up out of its line, fade it in, pop it in or type it. When the last one lands the element is the real text again: selectable, crisp and styled by your CSS. Text on screen when the page opens is hidden until the effect is ready and then plays the same way; if that takes over 3 seconds it shows as it is. With the scroll trigger such text stays as it is until scrolling reaches it.
target: any element with text: a heading, a paragraph, a link. Not img, video, canvas, svg or form fields. Any font-stretch, font-variation-settings and font-feature-settings draw as on the page when the font comes from a readable @font-face (same origin, or a stylesheet served with CORS such as Google Fonts); otherwise such text stays as it is, as does text with text-shadow, a text stroke, background-clip: text or vertical writing

params.name: by
params.description: Unit that moves as one; over 1500 letters it moves by words, over 1500 words by lines.

params.name: trigger
params.description: view plays when the text enters; scroll ties it to the scroll position, both ways.

params.name: motion
params.description: rise lifts each unit from below its baseline, tipped back and blurred, for most headings; mask slides it up out of its own line as if from behind an edge, the editorial look; fade fades it in place, coming into focus by blur, for body text; pop grows it from its middle with a slight overshoot, for a playful brand; type shows it at once when its turn comes, like a typewriter (set stagger to the time per unit).

params.name: duration
params.description: Time one unit takes to land; type ignores it.

params.name: stagger
params.description: Delay between neighboring units in reading order.

params.name: delay
params.description: Wait after the trigger, for a cascade.

params.name: rise
params.description: How far below its place a unit starts, with rise.

params.name: tilt
params.description: How far a unit starts tipped back around its baseline, with rise.

params.name: blur
params.description: How blurred a unit starts with rise and fade; 0 for sharp.

params.name: threshold
params.description: Share of the element height that must be in view, above the bottom tenth of the viewport, before it plays.

frames.note: Only while units move, and with the scroll trigger while scrolling; none at rest.

reducedMotion.note: Off: the text is shown as it is, and the engine does not load for it.

presence.note: Leaving a page, the units go again in reverse order; entering, they rise in order. A flight to a text element lands on the DOM text.

touch: The same as with a mouse: it follows the scroll.

notes.low: No blur, and the text is rastered at 1 device pixel per CSS pixel instead of 2.

cost.gpu: One instanced draw of a quad per unit, one texture read per pixel.
cost.memory: A canvas of the text at twice its CSS size with mip levels, kept while the element lives: about 2.5 MB for a 1200 x 200 heading.

name: scramble
summary: Headings and labels decode into place: each letter cycles through random glyphs before it settles.
looks: When the text scrolls into view, its letters appear one after another as random glyphs that flicker a few times a second and then lock into the real letters, left to right like a terminal decoding a message. Other motions show every letter scrambled at once and settle them in a random order, or add a brief red and cyan split and jitter, like a glitching screen. When the last letter settles the element is the real text again: selectable, crisp and styled by your CSS. With the hover trigger a label stays as it is and scrambles again each time the pointer or keyboard focus reaches it.
target: a heading, a label, a link or a button with text. Not img, video, canvas, svg or form fields

params.name: motion
params.description: decode settles letters left to right, each scrambling in turn, for most headings; random scrambles every letter at once and settles them in a random order, for numbers and codes; glitch decodes with a red and cyan split and a jitter, for a louder tech look.

params.name: by
params.description: letter gives each letter its own turn; word lets the letters of a word settle together.

params.name: trigger
params.description: view plays when the text enters; scroll ties it to the scroll position, both ways; hover plays it each time the pointer or focus reaches it.

params.name: chars
params.description: Glyph set: mixed, latin, upper, digits, hex, binary, symbols, or your own string.

params.name: duration
params.description: Time one letter scrambles before it settles.

params.name: stagger
params.description: Delay between neighboring letters or words in their turn order.

params.name: delay
params.description: Wait after the trigger, for a cascade.

params.name: cycle
params.description: Time each random glyph shows before the next one.

params.name: threshold
params.description: Share of the element height in view, above the bottom tenth, before it plays.

params.name: seed
params.description: Picks the random glyphs and order; the same seed plays the same way.

frames.note: Only while letters scramble, and with the scroll trigger while scrolling; none at rest.

reducedMotion.note: Off: the text is shown as it is, and the engine does not load for it.

presence.note: Leaving a page, the settled letters scramble again in reverse order and go; entering, they decode in order.

touch: The same as with a mouse, except that the hover trigger needs keyboard focus on touch.

notes.low: The text and the glyphs are rastered at 1 device pixel per CSS pixel instead of 2.

cost.gpu: Two instanced draws of a quad per letter, one or three texture reads per pixel.
cost.memory: A canvas of the text at twice its CSS size with mip levels, and a small sheet of the glyph set, kept while the element lives.

name: marquee
summary: An endless ticker of a row of text, logos or images that speeds up and leans as the page scrolls.
looks: The content of the element runs sideways in a seamless loop, with copies following each other at an even gap, and fades out softly at both ends. Scrolling the page pushes it faster and tips it forward in the direction it runs; it can also turn around when the page scrolls up. It slows to a stop under the mouse or keyboard focus and picks up again after. The content stays in the page once, so screen readers read it once while the copies you see are drawn by the GPU.
target: a row of text, logos, inline SVGs or images laid out on one line, such as a flex row. Not img, video, canvas, svg or form fields

params.name: direction
params.description: left runs the content to the left; right runs it to the right.

params.name: speed
params.description: Pace without scrolling; 0 moves it only while the page scrolls.

params.name: gap
params.description: Extra space between copies, on top of the row gap (1em for plain text).

params.name: boost
params.description: Extra travel per pixel of page scroll; 0 ignores the scroll.

params.name: skew
params.description: Lean into the motion during a fast scroll; 0 keeps it upright.

params.name: reverse
params.description: Scrolling up turns the ticker around until the page scrolls down.

params.name: pause
params.description: Slows to a stop under the mouse or keyboard focus.

params.name: fade
params.description: Soft edge at each side, as a share of the width; 0 for hard edges.

frames.note: Up to 60 a second while it moves and is on screen; none off screen, paused or at speed 0 without scrolling.

reducedMotion.note: Static: the row stands still with its copies, and scrolling does not move it.

presence.note: Fades with the page.

touch: The same, without the pause: a finger on it scrolls the page and pushes the ticker.

notes.low: The content is drawn at 1 device pixel per CSS pixel.

cost.gpu: One quad over the element, one texture read per pixel.
cost.memory: A canvas of one copy of the content at the screen density, without mip levels: about 1.4 MB for a 3000 x 60 row at 2x.

name: video-text
summary: The letters of a headline become a window onto a video or a photo, while the page shows around them.
looks: The headline keeps its font, size and layout, but its letters show a muted video playing inside them, framed over the text as a whole, and the page’s own background shows around and between them. Once the first frame is ready the letters turn from their CSS color into the video in about half a second. A photo works the same way and stands still. The text stays in the DOM for screen readers, search and selection.
target: a heading or short text in a large, heavy font. Not img, video, canvas, svg or form fields

params.name: src
params.description: URL of a video, or several by spaces such as WebM then MP4; an image URL shows a photo.

params.name: fit
params.description: cover fills every letter; contain shows all of it, some letters empty; fill stretches it.

params.name: fps
params.description: Most frames drawn a second while the video plays; 0 holds the first frame.

params.name: loop
params.description: Plays the video again from the start; off holds its last frame.

params.name: dim
params.description: How far the picture inside the letters goes dark, for contrast on a light page; 0 keeps it as is.

frames.note: Only while the video plays and the text is on screen, at most fps a second, and for half a second as the picture fades in; none for a photo or a paused video.

reducedMotion.note: The video stands on its first frame and does not play; the letters still show it.

presence.note: The text fades with the page.

touch: The same as with a mouse: the video plays while the text is on screen.

notes.low: At most 24 frames a second, and the text is rastered at 1 device pixel per CSS pixel.

cost.gpu: One quad over the text: a texture read of the text and one of the video per pixel.
cost.memory: A canvas of the text at twice its CSS size with mip levels, and one video frame. A video of 1280 px wide or less is enough for a headline.

name: wave

looks: When the heading scrolls into view a wave runs through it from left to right: each letter lifts and settles in turn, like a crowd doing the wave in a stadium. Other axes rock the letters, swell them or tip their tops towards you. With the loop trigger the letters float on an endless wave instead, for a festival title or a playful brand line. params.name: wavelength

params.name: speed
params.description: Loop trigger: waves per second; 0 holds the wave still.

params.name: duration
params.description: View, hover and scroll: time one letter takes to rise and settle.

params.name: stagger
params.description: View, hover and scroll: delay between neighboring letters.

params.name: delay
params.description: Wait after the trigger, for a cascade.

params.name: threshold
params.description: Share of the element height in view, above the bottom tenth, before it plays.

params.name: fps
params.description: Loop trigger: most frames per second; the pulses always run at full rate.

presence.note: The copy fades with the page.

name: split-flap
summary: A departure board: each character flips through a drum of letters to its own, on view and whenever the site changes the text.
looks: Every letter sits on a dark tile split across the middle. When the board comes into view the top half of each tile falls over its hinge again and again, showing the next letter of the drum, until it lands on the right one; letters further along the drum take longer, so the line settles unevenly like a real station board. When your code changes the text, only the characters that changed flip to their new letters. The plain style flips the letters without tiles and hands back to the real text at rest.
target: a short line of text: a destination, a status, a price, a time, a menu item. Not img, video, canvas, svg or form fields

params.name: style
params.description: tiles draws each character on a split tile in the tile color, also at rest; plain flips the letters alone and shows the real text at rest.

params.name: motion
params.description: drum walks the drum in order, so each letter takes as many flips as it is far from its target, up to flips; random shows flips random faces on every letter, so they land together.

params.name: trigger
params.description: view flips in from blank when the text enters, then on every change; change shows the text as it is and flips only when it changes.

params.name: chars
params.description: Characters on the drum: board (A to Z, digits and . , : - / &), letters, digits, time, or your own string in order. Characters not on it are dropped in at the end of the flips.

params.name: duration
params.description: Time of one flip; 0 swaps the letters without flipping.

params.name: flips
params.description: Most flips per character; 0 or 1 flips straight to the new letter.

params.name: stagger
params.description: Delay between neighboring characters that flip.

params.name: delay
params.description: Wait after the text enters, for a cascade.

params.name: threshold
params.description: Share of the element height in view, above the bottom tenth, before it plays.

params.name: tile
params.description: Color of the tiles; the letters take the color of the text.

params.name: gap
params.description: Space between neighboring tiles.

params.name: shade
params.description: Shadow on a turning flap, the slit and the lighter top half; 0 is flat.

params.name: seed
params.description: Picks the random faces; the same seed plays the same way.

frames.note: Only while flaps turn; none at rest.

reducedMotion.note: Static: the tiles stay, and new text shows at once without flips. The plain style is the text as it is.

presence.note: The copy fades with the page.

touch: The same as with a mouse.

notes.low: The letters are drawn at 1 device pixel per CSS pixel instead of 2.

cost.gpu: One instanced draw of three quads per character, one texture read per pixel.
cost.memory: A small sheet of the drum and the letters of the text, kept while the element lives.

name: counter
summary: Stats count up to their value on real 3D mechanics: odometer drums, slot machine reels or flip cards.
looks: When a number such as 12,480 or $4.2M scrolls into view, each of its digits sits on a drum that turns in 3D: digits curve over the top and bottom of the drum, foreshortened and darker as they turn away, with a soft sheen and seams between the drums. The value counts up from 0 like a mechanical odometer, the last drum overshooting its digit and settling back. The slot style spins deeper reels behind window frames, blurred while they spin, and lands them one by one from right to left with a bounce; the flip style drops the top half of each card about its hinge towards the viewer until the digit lands. The text around the number and its separators stay flat. When the digits land, the drums or cards fold back into the page and the element is its own text again.
target: a heading, paragraph or span holding one number, with any text before and after it, such as $4.2M, 99.9% or 12,480 swimmers

params.name: style
params.description: odometer turns flush drums in a row, for stats sections; slot spins deep reels behind window frames and lands them right to left, for totals and prices; flip drops flip cards through the digits, for dashboards and scores.

params.name: trigger
params.description: view counts once when the number enters; scroll ties the count to the scroll, both ways.

params.name: duration
params.description: Time of the count; with slot and flip, until the last digit lands.

params.name: from
params.description: Value the count starts from, at most what the digits of the number can hold.

params.name: stagger
params.description: Delay between neighboring digits landing, for slot and flip.

params.name: delay
params.description: Wait after the trigger, for a row of stats.

params.name: threshold
params.description: Share of the element height in view, above the bottom tenth, before it counts.

frames.note: Only while the digits turn and fold back, and with the scroll trigger while scrolling; none at rest.

reducedMotion.note: Off: the number is shown as it is, and the engine does not load for it.

presence.note: Entering a page the number counts up from its start value; leaving, it counts back down to it.

touch: The same as with a mouse: nothing reads the pointer.

notes.low: The text and the digits are rastered at 1 device pixel per CSS pixel instead of 2.

cost.gpu: A strip of 24 quads per digit with ten texture reads per pixel for the motion blur, a quad per letter around the number.
cost.memory: A canvas of the text at twice its CSS size and a small sheet of the digits, kept while the element lives.

name: magnet
summary: Letters become lit 3D slabs that react to the pointer: they push away, turn toward it, rise like a dock or tumble, and spring back.
looks: As the pointer comes near a heading or a link, the letters around it lift off the page as thin glossy slabs. By default they are pushed away and turn their faces from the pointer, the rest of the line making room so no letter runs over its neighbor, and their sides and beveled edges catch the light and each casts its own soft shadow on the page. Other styles turn the letters to face the pointer, raise the ones under it toward the viewer while their neighbors make room, like the macOS dock seen in perspective, or toss them apart, each spinning its own way. Every letter rides a spring, so when the pointer moves on they wobble back into place and the element is the real text again.
target: a heading, a link, a button label or a short line of text. Not img, video, canvas, svg or form fields

params.name: style
params.description: repel pushes letters off and turns their faces away from the pointer; attract turns them to face it and draws them in; lift raises the letters under it toward the viewer while neighbors make room; scatter tosses them up and apart, each spinning its own way.

params.name: radius
params.description: Reach of the pointer in em of the text, so a link and a headline feel alike.

params.name: strength
params.description: How far letters move, rise and turn; 0 leaves them in place.

params.name: rotate
params.description: Largest turn of a letter in 3D at the pointer; 0 keeps faces to the viewer.

params.name: stiffness
params.description: Pull of each letter toward where it goes; higher is snappier.

params.name: damping
params.description: Friction of the springs; lower wobbles longer, about 26 does not wobble.

frames.note: Only while letters move toward the pointer or spring back; none at rest.

reducedMotion.note: Off: the text stays as it is, and the engine does not load for it.

presence.note: Fades with the page.

touch: A finger pressed on the text moves the letters around it until it lifts or the page starts to scroll.

notes.low: The letters are rastered at 1 device pixel per CSS pixel instead of 2.

cost.gpu: Two instanced draws: five quads per letter for its face and sides, one for its shadow, two texture reads per pixel.
cost.memory: An atlas of the letters at twice their CSS size with room for the shadows, and a relief map of the same size, kept while the element lives.

name: text-glitch
summary: A heading glitches in depth: it breaks into slabs that jump at the viewer, then snaps back flat.
looks: For about two thirds of a second the text breaks into horizontal slabs that jump sideways and towards or away from the viewer, turning in real perspective. Red and cyan layers sit at different depths behind and in front of the letters, so they part as the line tilts. The slice style turns struck slabs into solid blocks with shaded sides; vhs leans the line back with a hologram of scanlines trailing behind it and bends it like worn tape. The pattern jumps twenty times a second; a burst hits twice, with a moment of lost signal between the hits where the text dims, then the element is the real text again, selectable and crisp.
target: a heading, a label, a link or a button with text. Not img, video, canvas, svg or form fields

params.name: style
params.description: rgb tilts the line and parts its color layers; slice extrudes blocks; vhs is a hologram.

params.name: trigger
params.description: hover on pointer, focus or tap; interval every few seconds; scroll with speed; load once.

params.name: strength
params.description: How many slabs break and how far they jump and turn; 0 keeps them in place.

params.name: split
params.description: How far the red and cyan layers part in depth and sideways; 0 for none.

params.name: slices
params.description: About how many slabs each line of text breaks into.

params.name: interval
params.description: Average time between bursts with trigger interval, varied by the seed.

params.name: duration
params.description: Length of one burst; from 0.4 s it hits twice with the signal lost between.

params.name: seed
params.description: Which glitch plays: the same seed gives the same one.

frames.note: Only during a burst, and with trigger scroll while the page scrolls fast; none at rest. A timer waits between interval bursts without drawing.

reducedMotion.note: Off: the text is shown as it is, and the engine does not load for it. Sudden flicker can trouble people sensitive to motion and flashing. With motion on, the text dims at most 3 times in any second, under the WCAG flash threshold.

presence.note: Leaving a page the slabs fly at the viewer and drop out one by one; entering they fall back into place.

touch: hover plays a burst on tap and on keyboard focus. The other triggers work the same as with a mouse.

notes.low: The text is rastered at 1 device pixel per CSS pixel instead of 2.

cost.gpu: One instanced draw of a quad per layer of a slab, one texture read per pixel; a block adds 14 layers to its slab, the hologram 7.
cost.memory: A canvas of the text at twice its CSS size with mip levels, kept while the element lives.

name: neon
summary: A heading becomes a 3D neon sign: round glass tubes that stutter on, light the wall and cast a shadow.
looks: The letters become round glass tubes mounted a little in front of the page. Lit, the gas glows white hot along the middle of each tube and saturated at its sides, a highlight runs along the glass, and the tubes throw a soft colored light onto the wall behind them, where their shadow falls too. When the sign comes into view its tubes stutter on one after another like a real sign warming up, and once lit it buzzes now and then. The light that casts the shadow sits above the screen, so the shadow shifts as the page scrolls; a mouse near the sign takes its place, the shadow swings away from it, the highlights slide along the tubes and the sign turns a little toward it. The outline style bends one thin tube along the edge of each letter instead of filling it.
target: a heading, a label or a short line of text, best on a dark background. Not img, video, canvas, svg or form fields

params.name: style
params.description: tube makes each stroke a round tube; outline bends a thin tube along the edge.

params.name: trigger
params.description: view turns on as it shows; hover lights on pointer, focus or tap; always stays lit.

params.name: color
params.description: Color of the gas and its light, any CSS color; empty uses the text color.

params.name: glow
params.description: Radius of the light thrown on the wall, in ems of the font size; 0 for none.

params.name: strength
params.description: Brightness of the light on the wall and around the tubes; 0 leaves bare tubes.

params.name: depth
params.description: How far the tubes stand off the wall, in ems; 0 mounts them flat on it.

params.name: shadow
params.description: Darkness of the shadow the tubes cast on the wall; 0 for none.

params.name: tilt
params.description: Largest turn of the sign toward a mouse near it, degrees; 0 keeps it still.

params.name: flicker
params.description: How often and how deep the lit sign buzzes and dims; 0 holds it steady.

params.name: broken
params.description: Share of the letters that keep stuttering and going dark; 0 for none.

params.name: seed
params.description: Picks the flicker, the broken letters and the turn-on; the same seed repeats.

frames.note: Full rate while tubes switch on or off and while the lamp or the sign follows the mouse, 30 a second while a tube flickers, none in between: a timer wakes the sign for its next flicker. With flicker and broken at 0 it draws nothing once lit, except on scroll.

reducedMotion.note: The sign is lit from the start: no turn-on, no flicker, no broken letters, the shadow does not follow the scroll or the mouse, and it draws no frames of its own.

presence.note: Leaving a page the tubes go dark from the last letter back and the glass fades; entering they light up in reading order.

touch: No mouse lamp and no turn: the light stays above the screen. With trigger hover a tap switches the sign on and off.

notes.low: The text is rastered at 1 device pixel per CSS pixel instead of 2, and the distance field at half that.

cost.gpu: Three instanced draws of a quad per letter (wall light and shadow, bloom, tubes), at most three texture reads per pixel; nothing is blurred on the GPU.
cost.memory: A canvas of the text at twice its CSS size, a distance field of it with its direction, and a small atlas of each letter’s light blurred once on the CPU.

name: assemble
summary: Thousands of lit particles fly out of the depth around the page and gather into a heading.
looks: When the heading scrolls into view, a cloud of small glossy beads drifts in front of and behind the page, larger and softer the closer it is to the viewer, then streams along curved paths into the shapes of the letters, left to right, and settles without overshoot. As each letter fills, the real text fades in over its particles, so the heading ends as selectable DOM text with no jump. Tiles that tumble and glint, or streaks of light, can stand in for the beads, and the cloud can rise from below, burst out of a point deep behind the heading or pour in from both sides. With the hover trigger the heading stays made of beads, and the ones under the pointer or a finger lift towards the viewer and spring back.

params.description: scatter starts from a cloud around the heading, in front of and behind the page; below rises from under it; center bursts out of a point deep behind its middle; edges pours in from both sides.

params.name: trigger
params.description: view gathers when the heading enters; scroll gathers it towards the middle of the viewport and scatters it again above; hover keeps it as beads the pointer lifts.

params.name: density
params.description: Particles per area of the glyphs; 2 doubles them, up to the tier limit.

params.name: dot
params.description: Size of a particle once it has landed.

params.name: duration
params.description: Flight time of one particle from its start to its place.

name: dust
summary: A heading crumbles into fine sand that lifts off the page and drifts away in depth as it scrolls out, or on a click.
looks: The text breaks into grains made of its own pixels, so the first grain to come loose looks exactly like the ink it leaves. A ragged edge sweeps across the heading from the side the wind blows to; behind it the grains lift off the page towards the viewer, tumble and catch a soft light from the upper left, and stream away along swirling paths, growing and blurring as they come closer and casting faint shadows on the page below. Other motions let the grains rise like ash or blow the heading apart into tiles that fly out of the page in every direction. Scrolling back gathers the sand into the heading again, and at rest the heading is plain DOM text.
target: a large heading, a short line of display text or a dismissible message. Not img, video, canvas, svg or form fields. Text with text-shadow, a text stroke, background-clip: text or vertical writing stays as it is

params.name: trigger

params.name: density

params.name: dot

params.name: duration

params.name: angle

params.name: turbulence
params.description: Strength of the swirls the grains ride; 0 lets them fly straight.

params.name: depth
params.description: How far the grains travel towards the viewer and back; 0 keeps them flat.

params.name: shadow
params.description: Darkness of the shadows lifted grains cast on the page; 0 turns them off.

params.name: seed
params.description: Picks the ragged edge, paths and sizes; the same seed blows the same way.

name: extrude
summary: A headline becomes a solid 3D block: beveled letters with lit side walls, seen in perspective, that turn toward the pointer.
looks: The letters keep their font and layout but gain real depth: each one is a block extruded behind its face, with a rounded bevel that catches the light, walls shaded by which way they face and darker toward the back, and a soft shadow on the page behind. The depth recedes in perspective, so letters far from the center show more of their sides. As the pointer moves, the block turns to face it and the light slides over the bevels; with scroll it turns as the heading crosses the viewport. Other styles stack the glyphs as paper layers in your colors, or draw a flat long shadow.

params.description: solid is a lit, beveled block; layers stacks paper cutouts; shadow is a flat long shadow.

params.name: by
params.description: pointer turns it toward the pointer; scroll turns it as the page scrolls; none holds it.

params.name: depth
params.description: How far the depth reaches behind the face at rest; a long shadow runs 5 times this.

params.name: layers
params.description: Number of paper layers behind the face in the layers style.

params.name: tilt
params.description: Largest turn of the block toward the pointer or with the scroll; 0 holds it.

params.name: light

params.name: color
params.description: Wall color for solid, paper base for layers, shadow color for shadow; empty derives it.

params.name: colors
params.description: Colors of the paper layers from front to back, repeated; empty uses darker shades.

frames.note: While the depth grows in once, while the pointer moves or the block settles after it, and while scrolling; none at rest.

presence.note: The block fades with the page.

name: shimmer
summary: A heading becomes polished chrome, gold, holographic foil or clear glass that catches the light as the pointer moves.
looks: Every letter gets a rounded bevel built from its own shape and is lit as a real material in a small photo studio: a bright sky over a sharp horizon, a dark floor, a softbox overhead and tall strips at the sides. The reflections slide over the letters as the pointer moves and the page scrolls, a light sweeps across them on hover, as they come into view or on a loop, and a soft shadow falls on the page beside them. Chrome and gold are mirror metals, holo is a rainbow foil whose colors shift with the viewing angle and glitter in fine points, and glass is clear in the middle with bright or dark rims and light gathered inside its edges.

params.name: style
params.description: chrome a mirror metal; gold a warm metal; holo a rainbow foil; glass clear tinted letters.

params.name: trigger
params.description: hover sweeps on pointer, focus or tap; loop every few seconds; view once; pointer a lamp.

params.name: colors

params.name: angle

params.description: Pace of the sweep and the loop; 0 never sweeps.

params.name: follow

params.name: shadow
params.description: Darkness of the soft shadow the letters cast on the page; 0 for none.

cost.memory: A canvas of the text at twice its CSS size and a half-float map of the bevel, built once on the CPU from a distance field of the letters.

name: rotator
summary: Words take turns in a headline on the faces of a real 3D cube, drum, split flap or folding strip.
looks: The word in the headline sits on a face of a solid shape. Every few seconds the shape turns in perspective to show the next word: a cube rolls up, a drum spins with the words above and below curving away, a split flap falls over its hinge, or a strip folds back into the page while the next one unfolds. Faces darken as they turn away from a lamp above the text and catch a glint as they pass it, and the line around the word eases to the new width. Between turns the word is plain text.
target: an inline element of a heading or paragraph whose children are the words, one element each, such as spans. Not img, video, canvas, svg or form fields

params.name: style
params.description: cube rolls a box; drum spins a wheel; flip drops a split flap; fold folds a paper strip.

params.name: trigger
params.description: interval turns on a timer; scroll scrubs the words with the scroll; hover turns on hover.

params.name: axis
params.description: x turns the words up and over; y turns them sideways, along the line.

params.name: interval
params.description: Time each word stays before the next turn, with trigger interval.

params.name: duration
params.description: Time one turn takes.

params.name: depth
params.description: Strength of the perspective; 0 turns the shape flat, without perspective.

params.name: shade
params.description: How much the lamp darkens and lights the turning faces; 0 keeps the text color.

params.name: pause
params.description: Holds the timer while the pointer is over the line or focus is in it.

params.name: loop
params.description: Starts over after the last word; false stops on it.

frames.note: Only while a word turns, and with trigger scroll while scrolling through a turn; none between turns: a timer wakes the next one.

reducedMotion.note: The words still change, but fade into each other in place over a third of a second, without turning.

presence.note: Between turns the word leaves and enters with the page; a turn under way fades with its copy.

touch: The same as with a mouse; with trigger hover a tap turns to the next word, and nothing pauses.

notes.low: The words are rastered at 1 device pixel per CSS pixel instead of 2.

cost.gpu: One instanced draw of two to six textured quads while a word turns; nothing between turns.
cost.memory: A small atlas of the words of the current turn at twice their CSS size, replaced each turn.

name: inflate
summary: Letters puff up into round 3D shapes, like balloons or soft clay, that dent and wobble under the pointer.
looks: Each letter swells into a soft, rounded volume, as if it were filled with air: straight strokes become round tubes, dots become domes and the joints of strokes bulge a little. A studio light from the upper left shades the volume, a glossy highlight runs along it and a soft shadow sits on the page under the letters. As the text comes into view the letters inflate from flat one after another with a springy overshoot. Where the pointer rests the skin dents in and nearby letters lean toward it; a press dents deeper, and on release the letters spring back with a wobble. The soft style looks like matte clay, and the jelly style like translucent gummy candy, clear at the rims and deeper in color where it is thick.
target: a heading, a label or the text inside a button, in a bold or display font. Not img, video, canvas, svg or form fields

params.name: style
params.description: balloon is glossy foil; soft is matte clay; jelly is clear gummy candy.

params.name: trigger
params.description: view inflates as it shows; hover inflates on pointer, focus or tap; always starts round.

params.name: color
params.description: Color of the letters, any CSS color; empty keeps the color of each letter.

params.name: depth
params.description: How far the letters puff out: 1 makes round tubes, 0 leaves them flat.

params.name: gloss
params.description: Strength of the highlights and of the sheen at the rims; 0 for none.

params.name: squish
params.description: How deep the pointer dents the letters under it; 0 turns the dent off.

params.name: tilt
params.description: Largest lean of the letters near the pointer, degrees; 0 keeps them upright.

params.name: duration
params.description: Time one letter takes to inflate, overshoot included.

params.name: stagger
params.description: Delay between neighboring letters as they inflate.

params.name: delay
params.description: Wait after the trigger, for a cascade.

params.name: threshold
params.description: Share of the element height in view, above the bottom tenth, before it plays.

frames.note: Full rate while letters inflate or deflate and while the dent and the lean follow the pointer and spring back; none at rest, under a still pointer or with the pointer away.

reducedMotion.note: The letters are round from the start and stay still: no inflating, no dent and no lean, and no frames of their own. With trigger hover the label switches between flat and round without motion.

presence.note: Leaving a page the letters go flat and fade; entering, they puff up again.

touch: A finger pressing the letters dents them and they spring back when it lifts; nothing follows a hover. With trigger hover a tap inflates the label and the next one lets it go flat.

notes.low: The text is rastered at 1 device pixel per CSS pixel instead of 2, and its field holds at most 600,000 texels instead of 1.6 million.

cost.gpu: Two draws: a grid of about one vertex per 3 CSS px for each letter, raised in the vertex shader, with six texture reads per pixel for the light, and one quad for the shadow.
cost.memory: A canvas of the text at twice its CSS size with mip levels, and a half-float field of it with a margin for the shadow, 8 bytes a texel, built once on the CPU in short steps.

name: ribbon
summary: A headline printed on waving 3D fabric: a flag in the wind, a twisting satin ribbon or slow rippling silk.

The folds are lit by their own normals, so the sides turned away from the light darken, crests catch a glossy highlight, and the cloth casts a soft shadow on the page that moves with it. A flag is pinned at its left edge and swings wider toward the free end; a ribbon runs one strip per line, and a twist rolls along it, turning the strip past edge-on to show its tinted back; silk ripples slowly while a sheen sweeps across. The pointer presses a dent into the cloth that follows it.

params.description: flag is pinned at the left; ribbon twists along each line; silk ripples with a sheen.

name: voxel

Each cube is lit from the upper left with a beveled edge, and the grooves between neighbors are darker. Once a column has landed the cubes flatten into the face of the text and the real text fades in over them, so the heading ends as selectable DOM text. Toy bricks with studs or flat retro voxels can stand in for the cubes; the voxels stay as they are, and cubes under the pointer pop out toward the viewer, lean out of the bump and spring back.

name: shatter
summary: A heading breaks into lit 3D shards that fly apart and tumble, then fly back together: on a click, on scroll, under the pointer or once in view.
looks: The text box cracks into pieces along seeded fracture lines that follow the letters, and each piece is a real slab with the heading printed on its face. On a click the cracks run out from the point of impact in rings, the pieces nearest it burst out first, and every piece flies off with its own spin, seen through the page camera so the ones coming toward the viewer grow. When the text comes back (hold above 0) the pieces slow down and hang in the air close to the heading, so the break stays in its box; with hold 0 they arc over and fall away under gravity. Turning pieces catch the light: faces brighten and darken, the cut edges glint, the walls show their thickness, and lifted pieces cast soft shadows on the page. Glass breaks into thin clear panes with green edges and reflections, stone into thick chunks with rough walls and a puff of dust, paper into torn scraps with pale fibers that flutter down and show their blank backs. After a pause the pieces fly back along their own paths and lock into place.
target: a large heading or short line of display text. Not img, video, canvas, svg or form fields. Text with text-shadow, a text stroke, background-clip: text or vertical writing stays as it is

params.description: Pull that bends the paths down; 0 lets the pieces drift off in a straight line.

params.name: depth
params.description: Thickness of a piece, times the thickness of its style; 0 makes flat pieces.

params.name: hold
params.description: Time the click trigger waits before the pieces fly back; 0 leaves the text gone.

params.name: seed
params.description: Picks the fracture lines, paths and spins; the same seed breaks the same way.

reducedMotion.note: The click trigger fades the text out instead, and back in after hold; the other triggers keep the text as it is.

presence.note: The pieces fade with the page.

touch: A tap breaks it with the click trigger; with the hover trigger a finger on the text lifts the pieces under it.

name: tunnel
summary: The phrases of a pinned section stand one behind another in real depth, and the scroll flies the camera through them.
looks: The first phrase sits where the page has it, and the next ones wait further back in the dark, smaller and fainter. Scrolling moves the camera forward: the phrase in front grows in perspective, blurs and passes the viewer, and the next one comes out of the distance and slows down to be read. In a tunnel the phrases wait on the floor and ceiling of a corridor drawn with faint lines and swing to face the reader as they arrive, and while one holds in focus nothing behind it crosses it; zoom flies straight through them; in a spiral they wait along a turning helix. A fast scroll streaks the letters toward the edges. At the end of the section the last phrase stays as plain text.
target: a block inside a pinned section, usually filling its sticky stage, whose children are the phrases, one element each, such as paragraphs. Not img, video, canvas, svg or form fields

params.name: style
params.description: tunnel lines the floor and ceiling of a corridor; zoom flies straight on; spiral turns along a helix.

params.name: depth
params.description: Distance between two phrases, in heights of the element.

params.name: perspective
params.description: Strength of the perspective: higher puts the eye closer, so phrases grow faster.

params.name: fade

params.name: blur
params.description: Blur of a phrase as it passes the viewer, at its nearest; 0 keeps it sharp.

params.name: streak
params.description: Motion streaks with the scroll speed, toward the edges; 0 turns them off.

params.name: twist
params.description: Turn of the helix from one phrase to the next, with style spiral.

params.name: lines
params.description: Draws the guide lines of the tunnel or the helix; zoom has none.

params.name: color
params.description: Color of the phrases and lines; currentColor keeps the text color.

frames.note: Only while the page scrolls, and a few more while the scroll speed settles with streaks on; none at rest.

reducedMotion.note: The effect does not run: the phrases stay as the page lays them out, one under another.

presence.note: The phrases fade with the copy as the page leaves or enters.

touch: The same as with a mouse: the scroll drives it.

notes.low: The phrases are rastered at 1 device pixel per CSS pixel instead of 2, without blur or streaks.

cost.gpu: One instanced draw of up to seven phrase cards with a 12-tap blur, and one draw of a few hundred thin line quads.
cost.memory: One atlas of every phrase at twice its CSS size, at most 4096 px a side.

name: emboss
summary: Letters pressed into or raised out of paper, leather, brushed metal, stone or plaster, lit by a light that follows the pointer.
looks: The element becomes a piece of material in its own background color, with the text as a real relief built from the shape of every letter: raised like a book cover, pressed in like a business card, printed into thick paper with ink in the bottom, or stood up on a wax seal. A lamp follows the pointer and drifts as the page scrolls, so the walls of the letters catch the light on one side and fall into shadow on the other, the letters cast soft shadows on the surface, and the fibres, grain, brushing or speckle of the material glint across the whole card. Small print stays printed in its color.
target: a card, cover, label or heading with a background color and short text in a bold font; text without a background is pressed into the page as it is. Not img, video, canvas, svg or form fields

params.name: style
params.description: emboss raised; deboss pressed in; letterpress an inked impression; stamp a wax seal.

params.name: material
params.description: paper fibres; leather pebble grain; metal brushed; stone speckled; plaster troweled.

params.name: depth
params.description: Height or depth of the relief in ems of the font size; 0 is flat.

params.name: bevel
params.description: Width of the sloped edge of each letter in ems; larger is softer and rounder.

params.name: light
params.description: Where the light comes from at rest as a CSS angle, 0 above and 90 right.

params.name: follow
params.description: How far the light moves toward the pointer; 0 keeps it at its angle.

params.name: grain
params.description: Strength of the material's own texture and mottle; 0 is smooth.

params.name: color
params.description: Ink or wax color, empty for the text color; given, it also inks emboss and deboss.

frames.note: None at rest: the relief is drawn once and stays. Full rate while the light settles after the pointer moves, and one frame per scroll while it drifts with the page.

reducedMotion.note: The light stays at its angle: it does not follow the pointer or drift with the scroll.

presence.note: The surface fades with the page.

touch: The light drifts with the scroll; a finger does not move it, so a tap or a swipe never flickers the relief.

notes.low: The relief is built at 1 px per CSS px instead of 2, and the shadow takes 8 steps toward the light instead of 16.

cost.gpu: One quad over the box; about twenty texture reads per pixel, sixteen of them for the shadow march toward the light.
cost.memory: A half-float relief of the text built once on the CPU from a distance field, a 512 px tile of the material per page and a canvas of the text.

name: pins
summary: The text becomes pin art: a field of metal pins around the words with the letters pushed out in relief.
looks: A field of thin metal pins seen through the page camera gathers around the words, their domed tips catching a studio light. The field follows the shape of the text and thins out at its edge, the last pins smaller and sunk into the page, so no plate or box shows. The pins inside the letters stand out toward the viewer, so the text rises as a crisp relief over the low pins, which sit dimmer and fainter in its shade; the raised pins cast soft shadows on the field and the page, and their shafts show at the edges in perspective. Pins are spaced in ems, so a letter is the same number of pins wide at any font size. As the heading comes into view the letters rise out of the flat field in a wave from left to right, overshooting a little, while the flat pins bob as the wave passes. The pointer presses the pins in under a soft circle, or pushes them out with press out, and they spring back with a wobble when it moves on. The bars style turns the pins into square bars, like a city skyline, and the domes style into round buttons, like a tactile display.
target: a heading or a short label in a bold or display font, 48 px and larger. Not img, video, canvas, svg or form fields

params.name: style
params.description: pins are thin metal pins; bars are square bars; domes are round plastic buttons.

params.name: press
params.description: in presses the pins under the pointer down; out pushes them up toward the viewer.

params.name: gap
params.description: Distance between the centers of neighboring pins in ems; it widens on long text to keep the pin count.

params.name: height
params.description: How far the letters stand out of the field; 0 leaves the field flat.

params.name: radius
params.description: Reach of the soft circle the pointer presses; 0 turns the pointer off.

params.name: color
params.description: Color of the pins, any CSS color; currentColor takes the text color.

params.name: duration
params.description: Time from the first pin rising to the last, the wave across the field included.

params.name: seed
params.description: Picks the small differences between pins and their timing.

frames.note: Full rate while the letters rise and while pressed pins move and spring back; none at rest, under a still pointer or with the pointer away. The relief stays drawn at rest.

reducedMotion.note: The letters stand in relief from the start and stay still: no rising wave, no pressing, and no frames of their own.

presence.note: Leaving a page the pins sink back into the field and fade; entering, they rise again.

touch: A finger pressing the field presses the pins under it and drags the soft circle along; they spring back when it lifts. Nothing follows a hover.

notes.low: At most 4,000 pins instead of 16,000, so the gap widens on long text, and fewer samples for the shadows.

cost.gpu: Two draws: one instanced mesh of lit pins, about 200 triangles each (18 for bars), with up to 18 reads of a small height texture per pixel for the shadows and the shade between pins, and one quad for the shadow on the page.
cost.memory: A canvas of the text at its CSS size and its distance field, read once on the CPU, and a half-float texture of one texel per pin, rewritten only while pins move.

name: melt
summary: Letters melt like wet paint, candle wax or liquid metal, running down in glossy drips that stretch, neck and let their drops fall.
looks: The shape of each letter turns liquid: its corners round off, its top sinks a little and its foot spreads, while drips run from the undersides of the strokes, widen into a bulb and now and then let a drop go that falls away below the text. The liquid is lit as a 3D surface with a round edge: sharp highlights along the rims, reflections of a small photo studio that slide as the page scrolls, and a soft shadow on the page. Drip is glossy paint in the color of the text, wax is warm and translucent with a pool along the baseline, and chrome is liquid mercury that ripples. The heading melts under the pointer and sets again when it leaves, follows the scroll, melts once as it comes into view and stays that way, or drips on a slow loop.
target: a large heading, a logo word or a short label in a bold font, with room below it for the drips. Not img, video, canvas, svg or form fields

params.name: style
params.description: drip glossy paint that runs; wax warm, slumping wax; chrome liquid mercury.

params.name: trigger
params.description: hover melts under the pointer; scroll follows the page; view melts once; loop drips on.

params.name: strength
params.description: How far the letters sag and the drips run; 0 keeps the shape and drips none.

params.name: drips
params.description: Number of drips across the text, spread along the undersides of the letters.

params.name: speed
params.description: Pace of the melt, of setting again after a hover and of the loop.

params.name: gloss
params.description: Strength of the highlights and the reflections; 0 is matte.

params.name: color
params.description: Color of the liquid, any CSS color; empty uses the color of the text.

params.name: seed
params.description: Picks where the drips hang and how long each one runs.

frames.note: With trigger hover and scroll the text is plain DOM at rest with no frames: full rate while it melts or sets under the pointer, one frame per scroll. View draws at full rate while it melts, then holds its look with none. Loop draws 30 frames a second while in view and none off screen.

reducedMotion.note: Hover and scroll leave the text as it is. View and loop show the melted look, drips hanging, without motion.

presence.note: The liquid fades with the page.

touch: With trigger hover a tap melts the spot under the finger, which sets again after a moment. Scroll, view and loop work the same as with a mouse.

notes.low: At most 8 drips, and the text is rastered at 1 device pixel per CSS pixel instead of 2.

cost.gpu: One quad over the text and the room below it; per pixel six evaluations of the shape, each a texture read or two and a loop over the drips near it.
cost.memory: A canvas of the text and a half-float distance field of it and of its rounded shape, at most 900,000 texels, built once on the CPU; a small heat map for the hover.

name: unfold
summary: A headline unfolds out of the page like paper: strips, a zig-zag band, letter cards or folded squares open in 3D.
looks: The text block is cut into pieces of paper hinged to each other. Before it opens you see the folded packet: off-white paper backs with a faint fiber, the letters showing through a little. As it comes into view the pieces swing open one after another in perspective, standing out of the page on the way: the side turned to the light brightens, folds darken toward the crease, and the raised paper casts a soft shadow on the page. Strips roll down line by line like a letter out of an envelope, an accordion stretches open sideways, each letter of cards stands up like a little card on its bottom edge, and origami opens squares folded corner to center. Once everything lies flat the heading is plain text again.
target: a heading or short text block in a large font. Not img, video, canvas, svg or form fields

params.name: style
params.description: strips rolls down; accordion stretches; cards stands letters up; origami opens squares.

params.name: trigger
params.description: view opens it once in view; scroll scrubs with the page; hover folds a little under the pointer.

params.name: bands
params.description: Strips, pleats or rows of squares; auto cuts one per line, or a pleat per two ems.

params.name: angle
params.description: How far each piece is folded before it opens; 180 lies folded flat.

params.name: duration
params.description: Time one piece takes to open.

params.name: stagger
params.description: Time between neighboring pieces, shortened so all start within 1.4 durations.

params.name: paper
params.description: Color of the backs of the pieces, the paper seen while folded.

params.name: shade
params.description: Strength of the shading on the faces and at the folds; 0 keeps flat colors.

params.name: delay
params.description: Wait between the trigger and the first fold.

params.name: threshold
params.description: Share of the heading in view that opens it with the view trigger, or starts the scrub.

frames.note: While the paper opens, and with the scroll trigger while scrolling through it; with the hover trigger while the pointer moves over it and the folds settle; none at rest.

reducedMotion.note: Off: the heading stays flat text.

presence.note: Leaving a page folds the paper back up, entering one unfolds it; at rest it leaves as text.

touch: With trigger hover a tap folds the pieces under the finger for a moment.

notes.low: The text is rastered at 1 device pixel per CSS pixel instead of 2.

cost.gpu: Three instanced draws of a quad per piece (lying flat, raised, and their shadows) while the paper moves; nothing at rest.
cost.memory: A canvas of the text at twice its CSS size with mip levels and a 256 px tile of paper fiber.

name: blinds
summary: A heading printed across real 3D slats that turn over in a wave, lit and casting shadows, to show it.
looks: The heading starts behind a closed panel of slats in a solid color, like a shutter or a flip sign. The slats turn over one after another, each a thin board in perspective whose painted back and edges catch the light, casting thin shadows on its neighbors and on the page, until the text lies flat and readable. Horizontal slats turn like venetian blinds, vertical ones like a shop shutter, and square tiles flip in a diagonal ripple like a stadium card display. The pointer nudges the slats near it, and the nudge runs on through the others before they settle. A second text can be printed on the backs, so the turn switches between two messages.
target: a heading or short text in a large font, on a solid page background. Not img, video, canvas, svg or form fields

params.name: style
params.description: horizontal turns strips like blinds; vertical turns upright slats; tiles flips cards.

params.name: trigger
params.description: view opens it once in view; scroll opens with the scroll; hover opens near the pointer.

params.name: slats
params.description: Slats per line of text, top to bottom; vertical slats and tiles get a like size.

params.name: gap
params.description: Space between neighboring slats while they turn; 0 closes them edge to edge.

params.name: duration
params.description: Time one slat takes to turn over.

params.name: stagger
params.description: Time between one slat starting to turn and the next, shortened on long waves.

params.name: delay
params.description: Wait before the first slat turns, with trigger view.

params.name: threshold
params.description: Share of the heading in view before it opens, with trigger view or scroll.

params.name: angle
params.description: Turn of the slats at rest with trigger hover: 180 closed on their back, 90 edge-on, 0 open.

params.name: light
params.description: Where the light comes from as a CSS angle, 0 above and 90 right.

params.name: back
params.description: Color of the slats' backs and edges; currentColor uses the text color.

params.name: reverse
params.description: Text printed on the backs, a second message on the closed panel; empty leaves them plain.

frames.note: Only while slats turn or settle after the pointer: with trigger view while the wave runs, with scroll while scrolling, with hover while slats follow the pointer; none at rest.

reducedMotion.note: Off: the text is shown as it is, and the engine does not load for it.

presence.note: Leaving a page the slats close again in reverse and fade; entering one, they open as the page comes in.

touch: View and scroll work the same; a moving finger nudges the slats. With trigger hover a tap opens every slat in a ripple from the finger, and the next tap closes them.

notes.low: The text is rastered at 1 device pixel per CSS pixel instead of 2.

cost.gpu: One instanced draw of a box per slat, up to 2048, and a shadow quad over the panel that tests up to nine slats per pixel; nothing at rest.
cost.memory: The text raster at twice its CSS size, the second text if any, and a small table of slat angles.

name: keycaps
summary: Each letter sits on a 3D mechanical keycap that presses down as if the word were typed, with a click under the pointer.
looks: The heading becomes a row of real 3D keycaps on a darker keyboard case, seen at an angle in the page perspective. Each cap is rounded, slightly dished and tapered, lit like plastic with a soft sheen, and the letter is printed on its top in the text color; a space becomes a wide space bar. When the heading comes into view the keys go down one after another as if someone typed the word: a quick press, a small bounce back and a flash of light on each. Keys under the pointer sink a little and a click sends one down hard. Modern sculpted caps with an accent key, beige retro caps, or dark caps with an RGB glow under them.

params.name: trigger

params.name: speed
params.description: Typing speed in keys per second.

params.name: sound

name: lens
summary: A glass reading lens follows the pointer over the text, magnifying it through real curved glass.
looks: A thick biconvex lens in a thin steel ring hovers over the page under the pointer. Every pixel is traced through both curved faces of the glass: the text comes up sharp and magnified in the middle, bends and splits into colors toward the rim, and the glass reflects a softbox and a dim studio, strongest at its edge. On the page beside it lies its shadow with the bright spot of light it focuses, and the shadow of its handle. The lens leans into its motion and settles with a little sway.
target: a block of text: an article, a column of fine print, a spec sheet or a caption; the lens shows its text over its solid background. Not img, video, canvas, svg or form fields

params.name: radius
params.description: Radius of the lens on screen in px.

params.name: zoom
params.description: Magnification in the middle of the lens; 1 is plain glass.

params.name: dispersion
params.description: How far the glass splits colors toward the rim; 0 has no color fringes.

params.name: thickness
params.description: How domed the glass is; thicker bends the rim more and hovers lower.

params.name: tilt
params.description: Largest lean into the motion in degrees; 0 keeps the lens level.

params.name: ease
params.description: Seconds the lens lags behind the pointer; 0 follows it exactly.

frames.note: None at rest and none while the lens is hidden. Full rate while it moves, leans, settles or fades in and out.

reducedMotion.note: The lens jumps with the pointer: no lag, no lean.

presence.note: The lens fades with the page.

touch: The lens appears while a finger is pressed on the text, held a little above the finger so it stays visible, and leaves when the finger lifts or the page scrolls.

notes.low: The text is rastered at the screen resolution instead of up to four times it.

cost.gpu: One quad around the lens and its shadow while it shows; three rays through the glass per pixel, one per color.
cost.memory: A canvas of the text at up to four device pixels per CSS px with mip levels, at most about six million pixels.

name: water
summary: A headline under water: the surface bends the letters, focuses dancing caustics on them and ripples under the pointer.
looks: The text lies a few centimeters under a real water surface. On the page the water is a puddle around the words with a wandering, rounded shore, shallow and nearly clear at its edge and deeper toward the letters, where its surface curls down to the page in a thin bright line; on an element with its own background it fills that box like a pool with walls. A height field simulated on the GPU, plus a slow swell, gives every point of the surface a normal: the letters are seen bent through it, the light it focuses draws a net of caustics over the letters and the floor, and the surface reflects a sky with a window and the glints of the sun by Fresnel. The water tints what lies deeper, red first. Moving the pointer drags a wake, a click drops a stone that rings out, rain lands in rings on its own, and ice is clear with frost and cracks, thinner over the letters so their color reads, until the pointer melts a clear patch that freezes over again.
target: a heading or short text in a large font, on a solid page color or with its own solid background, with padding of about a third of an em for the puddle. Not img, video, canvas, svg or form fields

params.name: style
params.description: pool is clear water with a moving swell; rain rings out under falling drops; ice is clear, frosted and cracked.

params.name: trigger
params.description: loop keeps the water moving; hover keeps it still until the pointer comes over it.

params.name: depth
params.description: How strongly the surface bends the letters seen through it; 0 keeps them straight.

params.name: caustics
params.description: Brightness of the light the waves focus on the letters and the floor; 0 turns it off.

params.name: ripples
params.description: Strength of the wake and the drops the pointer makes; 0 leaves the water alone.

params.name: rain
params.description: Raindrops a second with the rain style; 0 stops the rain.

params.name: damping
params.description: How fast ripples die out; 0 lets them run and bounce for a long time.

params.name: tint
params.description: Depth of the water color over the letters and the page; 0 is perfectly clear.

frames.note: With trigger loop, 30 frames a second while on screen (ice: only while a melted patch refreezes or ripples run). With hover, 30 a second while the pointer is over and the ripples settle, none at rest: the still water stays drawn.

reducedMotion.note: The water stays still: the swell holds its shape, there are no ripples, rain or melting, and the still water stays drawn.

presence.note: The water fades with the page.

touch: There is no wake without a mouse. A tap drops a ripple and, with hover, wakes the swell or the rain for a moment; on ice it melts a patch.

notes.low: The text is rastered at 1 device pixel per CSS pixel instead of 2 and the simulation grid is coarser.
notes.medium: The simulation grid is a little coarser.

cost.gpu: Two small half-float render targets of a few hundred cells a side, stepped about 60 times a second with nine reads per cell while waves run. The surface reads the simulation nine times and the letters once per pixel, plus the ice map on ice.
cost.memory: A canvas of the text at twice its CSS size with mip levels, two small simulation targets, a small half-float map of the shore of the puddle built once on the CPU and, for ice, a map of frost and cracks at about the size of the box.

name: fire
summary: The letters burn: flames rise from their tops, sparks drift up in depth and the firelight flickers on the page.
looks: Flames rise from the tops of the strokes that face open air, in a plume built from the shape of the letters: white-yellow where they leave the strokes, orange higher up, red at the tips, swaying and torn into tongues by turbulence carried up through them, taller over one letter and lower over the next as the fire breathes. Over the strokes the flames thin out, so the text stays readable. The tops of the letters glow like embers, their faces warm toward the fire and darken with soot where it burned. A few sparks rise in front of and behind the letters and cool from yellow to red as they climb. The firelight flickers on the page around the text in step with the flames, and the letters cast a soft shadow below. The embers style turns the letters into hot coals with light in their cracks and low flames; the candle style puts one calm, swaying flame on top of each letter.
target: a heading, a label or a short line of text, best on a dark background. Not img, video, canvas, svg or form fields

params.name: style
params.description: flame burns tall; embers makes glowing coals; candle lights one calm flame per letter.

params.name: trigger
params.description: loop burns on; hover lights near the pointer; view flares up once; scroll follows the page.

params.name: strength
params.description: Brightness of the flames, the sparks and the firelight; 0 puts the fire out.

params.name: height
params.description: Height of the flames over the letters, in ems; embers and candle keep theirs lower.

params.name: speed
params.description: Pace of the flames and the sparks; 0 holds the fire still.

params.name: embers
params.description: Sparks in the air at once; candle sends up a third as many, 0 for none.

params.name: color
params.description: Tint of the fire, any CSS color, such as a blue gas flame; empty for natural fire.

params.name: char
params.description: How dark the flames scorch the tops of the letters, recovering after; 0 for none.

params.name: seed
params.description: Picks the shape of the flames, the sparks and where the fire catches first.

frames.note: 30 a second while the fire burns and is on screen, none off screen. Hover and view draw nothing once the fire has died down and the char has faded, and view with embers stops once the coals settle; scroll draws while the text burns.

reducedMotion.note: A still warm glow: the letters lit and the page warm around them, no moving flames and no sparks. Candles stand still, coals keep their glow, and nothing is drawn after.

presence.note: Leaving a page the fire dies down and the letters fade with it; entering they catch fire again.

touch: With trigger hover a tap lights the letters around it for a moment; focus on the element or its link lights them all.

notes.low: At most 10 sparks, flames with less turbulence, and the text rastered at 1 device pixel per CSS pixel.

cost.gpu: A quad over the letters, one over the air above them for the flames (seven texture reads a pixel), one for the firelight around the text (two reads), and one small quad per spark or candle. Pixels with nothing to add are discarded.
cost.memory: A canvas of the text, a distance field of it, the plume the flames rise in, a small texture of the firelight and one of the heat of each letter.

name: physics
summary: Playful gravity type: the letters of a heading become thick lit 3D tiles that fall, bounce, tumble and pile up, can be thrown with the pointer, and stand back up.
looks: Each letter turns into a solid tile cut in the shape of its glyph, as thick as the depth says, with beveled edges and walls that catch the light. When the heading falls, the tiles drop to the bottom of their container, bounce, tip over and tumble about all three axes, seen through the page camera, and come to rest in a pile, lying on their faces or leaning on each other, each casting a soft shadow on the page and the floor. The drop style collapses the heading where it stands, scatter bursts the letters outward so they settle across the floor, and stack drops them in from above one by one into their places with a bounce. A loose letter can be grabbed, dragged and thrown. On demand the letters fly back up and the heading is plain text again.
target: a large heading or a short line of display text, in a container with room below it. Not img, video, canvas, svg or form fields

params.name: style
params.description: drop collapses the heading into a pile; scatter bursts the letters apart; stack drops them in one by one.

params.name: trigger
params.description: view falls once in view; click toggles on a click; scroll falls when scrolled past; hover knocks letters.

params.name: gravity
params.description: Pull of gravity, 1 is about earth for the page; 0 lets the letters float.

params.name: bounce
params.description: How much of its speed a letter keeps when it hits the floor or another letter.

params.name: friction
params.description: Grip between letters and the floor; 0 lets them slide like ice.

params.name: depth
params.description: Thickness of a tile in em of its font size; 0 draws flat letters.

params.name: throw
params.description: Strength of a throw with the pointer; 0 turns grabbing and knocking off.

params.name: container
params.description: Selector of an ancestor whose box the letters fall in; empty keeps the heading’s own box.

frames.note: While letters fall, fly, hop or are dragged; none once the pile has settled or the heading stands upright.

reducedMotion.note: Off: the heading stays upright as plain text, and the engine does not load for it.

presence.note: Fades with the page.

touch: A finger drags and throws a loose letter without scrolling the page; in the hover trigger a tap knocks a letter off.

notes.low: The letters are rastered at 1 device pixel per CSS pixel instead of 2 and the march through each tile takes 8 steps instead of 24.
notes.medium: The march through each tile takes 14 steps instead of 24.

cost.gpu: One instanced draw of a box per letter, marched to the glyph in up to 24 texture reads per pixel, and two instanced draws of shadows.
cost.memory: An atlas of the letters at twice their CSS size with room for the shadows, and a relief map of the same size.

name: smoke
summary: A heading condenses out of drifting volumetric smoke as it comes into view, or dissolves into it as it leaves.
looks: Smoke drifts in from below, swirls and thickens into the shapes of the letters, and the letters sharpen out of it until the plain text takes over. Dissolving, the letters soften and break up while plumes curl off their tops and rise away. The smoke is a real volume with depth: it is lit from behind and above, so thin wisps glow at their edges and the thick parts fall into their own shadow, and its layers shift against each other as the page scrolls. Styles give grey-white smoke for dark pages, a soft pale fog for light ones, or ink blooming in water in the color of the text.
target: a large heading or a short line of display text. Not img, video, canvas, svg or form fields. Text with text-shadow, a text stroke, background-clip: text or vertical writing stays as it is

params.description: smoke is grey-white smoke lit from behind, for dark pages; mist is a soft pale fog for light pages; ink blooms in the color of the text, like ink in water.

params.name: trigger
params.description: view condenses the heading when it comes into view, a first-screen heading included; scroll condenses it toward the middle of the viewport and dissolves it as it leaves; hover lets wisps curl off the letters under the pointer; loop keeps smoke rising off the letters.

params.name: density

params.name: speed

params.name: rise

params.name: turbulence
params.description: Strength of the swirls; 0 lets the smoke drift without curling.

params.name: duration
params.description: Time the view trigger takes to condense, and a hover wisp takes to settle.

params.name: color
params.description: Any CSS color for the smoke; empty uses grey-white for smoke, a pale fog for mist or the text color for ink.

params.name: seed
params.description: Picks the pattern of the swirls; the same seed drifts the same way.

presence.note: Leaving a page, the heading dissolves up into smoke; entering, it condenses out of it.

notes.medium: 12 steps with one step toward the light.

name: prism
summary: Letters become crystal: their edges split a light into a crisp spectrum that slides around them as the light moves.
looks: The text turns into bevelled glass in its own color, standing a little off the page. The face stays crisp ink; across each bevel the glass bends the view outward, and every color by its own amount, so the edge of the ink splits into a clean spectrum, as through a prism. Sharp highlights and thin lines of light caught inside the edges follow a lamp, and where a bevel faces away from it the light leaves in a thin saturated spectrum along the contour, with a fainter one landing on the page just past the letter. The rainbows gather near the lamp and slide around the curves as it moves: it follows the pointer, sweeps with the scroll, orbits slowly or passes once as the text comes into view.
target: a large heading or short display line in a bold font, on a plain background. Not img, video, canvas, svg or form fields

params.name: style
params.description: prism round glass with smooth spectra; crystal cut facets that flash colors; diamond more facets and fire.

params.name: trigger
params.description: pointer follows the pointer; scroll sweeps with the scroll; loop orbits; view passes once.

params.name: dispersion
params.description: How far the colors pull apart; 0 keeps the light white, with no rainbow.

params.name: spread

params.name: strength

params.name: bevel
params.description: Width of the bevel along every edge in ems; larger is rounder glass.

params.name: light
params.description: Where the light comes from at rest as a CSS angle, 0 above and 90 right.

params.name: follow
params.description: How far the light moves toward the pointer or with the scroll; 0 holds it.

params.name: fps
params.description: Frame rate of the loop; 0 holds the light still.

frames.note: None at rest: the glass and its spectra stay drawn. Full rate while the light settles after the pointer moves, one frame per scroll with trigger scroll, `fps` frames a second on a loop while in view, and a short sweep on view.

reducedMotion.note: The light stays at its angle and the spectra hold still.

presence.note: The glass and its light fade with the page.

touch: A finger does not move the light, so a tap or a swipe never flickers it; the scroll and loop triggers work as on desktop.

notes.low: The glass is built at 1 px per CSS px instead of 2, the light is split into 5 colors instead of 7, and the loop runs at most 24 frames a second.

cost.gpu: One quad over the text and a margin around it; about 25 texture reads per pixel, three per color of the split light.
cost.memory: A half-float relief of the text built once on the CPU from a distance field, and a canvas of the text.

name: hologram
summary: A heading becomes a 3D hologram: projected from a glowing emitter, built of slices in depth, crossed by scan lines.
looks: A small emitter disc lies below the text, tipped toward you, with a lit ring, a turning ring of dashes and a bright core; it lights the page around it and throws a faint cone of light up through the text. The letters float in front of the page as several translucent slices stacked in depth: the front one solid and bright, the ones behind showing only the edges, so the text has volume. Fine scan lines cross it, a brighter band sweeps up through it, rows shimmer sideways, the color splits into red and blue fringes at the edges, and now and then the projection stutters or a band tears sideways. It sways slowly a few degrees and tips toward a pointer near it, and the parallax between the slices shows the depth. The card style mounts the slices on a dark holographic trading card with a foil border and a glossy foil in front: tipping it with the pointer shifts the slices against each other and sweeps a rainbow sheen across, and it keeps its last pose. The ghost style drops the projector: a cool, pale apparition that fades in from noise, drifts back and forth in depth and trails echoes behind it.
target: a heading, a label or a short line of text, best on a dark background. Not img, video, canvas, svg or form fields

params.name: style
params.description: projector stands on an emitter; card sits on a foil card that tilts; ghost trails echoes.

params.name: trigger
params.description: view scans in as it shows; hover powers up on pointer, focus or tap; loop shimmers all the time.

params.name: color
params.description: Color of the projection and its light, any CSS color; empty uses cyan (ghost: ice blue).

params.name: layers
params.description: Slices stacked in depth; 1 draws a flat projection.

params.name: depth
params.description: Depth of the stack of slices, in ems of the font size.

params.name: scan
params.description: Strength of the scan lines, the sweep and the row shimmer; 0 for a clean projection.

params.name: flicker
params.description: How often the projection stutters, drops out or tears; 0 holds it steady.

params.name: sway
params.description: Largest slow turn of the hologram, degrees; 0 keeps it still.

params.name: tilt
params.description: Largest tip toward a pointer near it, degrees (card: 1.8 times); 0 ignores it.

frames.note: trigger view: full rate while it scans in (about 1.5 s), then none. hover: 30 a second while powered up, full rate while powering up or down, none at rest. loop: 30 a second while on screen, none off screen. Full rate while it tips toward the pointer.

reducedMotion.note: A still hologram at full power: no scan-in, no sweep, no shimmer, no flicker, no sway, no tip; it draws no frames of its own.

presence.note: The projection fades with the page.

touch: No tip toward the pointer. With trigger hover a tap powers it up and down.

notes.low: The text is rastered at 1 device pixel per CSS pixel instead of 2.

cost.gpu: Four draws: the light on the page, the emitter, the cone and one instanced quad per slice with five texture reads per pixel.
cost.memory: A canvas of the text at twice its CSS size, with its mip levels for the glow.
